  • Zero trust on AWS: identity everywhere (IAM), encrypt everywhere (TLS/KMS), log everything (CloudTrail/VPC Flow Logs).

questions.title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture
questions.scenario: A B2B SaaS company serves 500 tenants ranging from 10-user startups to 10,000-user enterprises. They need: tenant data isolation, per-tenant resource quotas, the ability to offer dedicated infrastructure to enterprise tenants, shared infrastructure for smaller tenants for cost efficiency, and a single code deployment that serves all tiers.
questions.questionText: Which multi-tenant architecture balances isolation, cost, and operational simplicity?

choices.text: Separate AWS accounts per tenant with shared deployment pipeline
Single account with tenant ID in every database record and application-level isolation only

Pool model for small tenants (shared DynamoDB with tenant partition key, shared EKS namespace), silo model for enterprise tenants (dedicated DynamoDB tables, dedicated EKS namespace with resource quotas), with tenant routing in API Gateway
Separate databases per tenant in a single RDS Multi-AZ instance with schema isolation

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The tiered approach (pool for small, silo for large) is the standard SaaS pattern — how do you implement it on AWS?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The hybrid pool/silo model optimizes cost for small tenants (shared infrastructure with logical isolation via partition keys and namespaces) while providing strong isolation for enterprise tenants (dedicated tables, dedicated compute with resource quotas). API Gateway with a tenant context Lambda determines the routing tier. A single EKS deployment serves all tenants — Kubernetes namespaces with ResourceQuotas provide compute isolation for enterprise tenants. DynamoDB partition keys provide data isolation in the pooled model.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• DynamoDB leading partition key = tenant ID ensures data is physically co-located and tenant-scoped queries are efficient.
  • EKS ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges enforce per-namespace CPU/memory limits for enterprise tenants.
  • API Gateway usage plans can provide per-tenant rate limiting and throttling.
  • AWS SaaS Factory reference architecture provides this pattern with terraform modules and reference implementations.

questions.title: VMware to AWS Migration
questions.scenario: A company runs 500 VMs on VMware vSphere 7 with vSAN storage. They want to migrate to AWS with minimal re-architecture. Phase 1 requires running VMware workloads natively on AWS (lift-and-shift), and Phase 2 will selectively modernize workloads to native AWS services. They need vMotion capability during Phase 1 for gradual migration without downtime.
questions.questionText: Which service enables native VMware workload execution on AWS with vMotion migration capability?

choices.text: VMware Cloud on AWS (VMC) with HCX for vMotion migration from on-premises
EC2 instances with VMware Workstation nested virtualization
AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) for all 500 VMs simultaneously
AWS Outposts with VMware vSphere installed locally

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service runs actual vSphere on dedicated hardware with migration tooling that supports live vMotion?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: VMware Cloud on AWS (VMC) runs a full VMware SDDC (vSphere, vSAN, NSX, vCenter) on dedicated AWS bare-metal infrastructure. VMware HCX provides bulk migration, vMotion (live migration without downtime), and network extension between on-premises vSphere and VMC. This enables Phase 1 (lift-and-shift with zero re-architecture) and Phase 2 (selective modernization by migrating individual VMs from VMC to native EC2 using AWS services). Existing VMware tools, scripts, and operations remain unchanged.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• VMC minimum is 2 hosts (i3.metal) with linear scaling; HCX supports live vMotion across 100+ ms latency.
  • VMC VMs can access native AWS services (S3, RDS, Lambda) via ENI connectivity to the connected VPC.
  • HCX supports bulk migration (100+ VMs simultaneously), live vMotion (zero downtime), and cold migration.
  • Phase 2 modernization uses VM Import/Export or Application Migration Service to move from VMC to native EC2.

questions.title: EBS Optimization Strategy
questions.scenario: A company's monthly EBS costs are $200,000. The bill breakdown shows: 40% is gp3 volumes (many at default 3000 IOPS/125 MBps), 30% is io2 volumes for databases, 20% is snapshot storage (5PB across 10,000 snapshots), and 10% is unused/detached volumes. Average gp3 utilization is 15% of provisioned IOPS.
questions.questionText: Which optimization strategy provides the greatest overall EBS cost reduction?

choices.text: Convert all io2 volumes to gp3 with increased IOPS
Enable EBS volume auto-scaling to dynamically adjust size based on usage
Move all workloads to instance store volumes for zero EBS cost
Delete detached volumes, implement EBS Snapshot Archive for snapshots older than 90 days, right-size gp3 volume sizes, and evaluate io2 Block Express for consolidation

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Address each cost segment: unused volumes (easy wins), snapshot sprawl (archive tier), volume right-sizing (reduce waste).

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Multi-pronged approach: Delete the 10% detached volumes (immediate $20K/month savings). Snapshot Archive costs 75% less than standard snapshots — archiving the 90%+ that are rarely accessed saves significant cost on the 5PB snapshot storage. Right-sizing gp3 volumes (reducing sizes where 85% of IOPS capacity is unused) reduces the 40% gp3 spend. Evaluating io2 Block Express may allow consolidating database IOPS requirements on fewer, larger volumes. This addresses all four cost segments systematically.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• EBS Snapshot Archive: $0.0125/GB/month vs standard $0.05/GB/month — 75% savings, with 24-72 hour restore time.
  • gp3 charges separately for size ($0.08/GB), IOPS above 3000 ($0.005/IOPS), and throughput above 125 MBps ($0.04/MBps).
  • io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS and 4,000 MBps — may replace multiple smaller io2 volumes.
  • AWS Trusted Advisor and Cost Explorer provide recommendations for unattached EBS volumes and underutilized volumes.

questions.title: Chaos Engineering Implementation
questions.scenario: A company wants to validate their application's resilience by systematically testing failure scenarios: AZ failures, service dependency outages, network latency injection, and resource exhaustion. They need controlled experiments that automatically abort if customer-impacting metrics breach thresholds, with findings documented for improvement.
questions.questionText: Which approach implements controlled chaos engineering experiments on AWS?

choices.text: AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) with experiment templates targeting specific resources, CloudWatch alarm-based stop conditions, and automated finding reports
Manually terminating EC2 instances and observing behavior through CloudWatch dashboards
Netflix Chaos Monkey deployed on EKS for random pod termination only
Load testing with Artillery to simulate high traffic and observe breaking points

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service provides managed chaos engineering with safety controls (stop conditions) built in?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) provides managed experiment templates that inject faults: AZ disruption, network latency/packet loss, CPU/memory stress, service API errors, and instance termination. Stop conditions linked to CloudWatch alarms automatically abort experiments when error rates or latency exceed thresholds — preventing customer impact. Experiment templates are versioned and reusable, supporting regular game days with documented findings for resilience improvement.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• FIS supports: EC2 (terminate, stop, reboot), EKS (pod/node disruption), RDS (failover), Network (latency, packet loss, blackhole).
  • Stop conditions evaluate every 10 seconds — experiments halt within 10-20 seconds of threshold breach.
  • FIS integrates with Systems Manager documents for custom fault injection actions.
  • Best practice: start with single-instance experiments, progress to AZ-level, then simulate region impairment.

questions.title: Secrets Management at Scale
questions.scenario: A company runs 300 microservices that collectively use 2,000 secrets (database credentials, API keys, certificates). Secrets must rotate automatically without application downtime, applications in different accounts need cross-account secret access, and the security team requires audit trails showing which service accessed which secret and when. Current approach uses environment variables in ECS task definitions.
questions.questionText: Which secrets management architecture provides rotation, cross-account access, and comprehensive auditing?

choices.text: HashiCorp Vault on EC2 with auto-unseal using KMS and audit backend to CloudWatch Logs
Parameter Store SecureString parameters with KMS encryption and IAM policies for access control
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation Lambda functions, resource-based policies for cross-account access, and CloudTrail for audit logging
Encrypted environment variables in ECS task definitions with manual rotation procedures

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service provides native automatic rotation, cross-account sharing, and full API-level audit logging?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Secrets Manager provides automatic rotation via Lambda functions (built-in support for RDS, Redshift, DocumentDB — custom Lambda for others). Resource-based policies enable cross-account access without credential copying. Integration with ECS/EKS references secrets at container startup without embedding in task definitions. CloudTrail logs every GetSecretValue call with source identity, enabling the security team to track exactly which service accessed which secret and when.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Secrets Manager rotation uses a 4-step Lambda: createSecret, setSecret, testSecret, finishSecret — enabling zero-downtime rotation.
  • ECS integrates natively with Secrets Manager — secrets are injected at task launch, and tasks get new values on next launch after rotation.
  • Resource policies support condition keys like aws:PrincipalOrgID for organization-wide access without listing each account.
  • Secrets Manager costs $0.40/secret/month + $0.05/10K API calls vs Parameter Store Advanced at $0.05/parameter/month.

questions.title: GraphQL API Architecture
questions.scenario: A social media application needs a GraphQL API that aggregates data from 8 different backend services (user profiles, posts, comments, likes, notifications, media, recommendations, analytics). Each resolver may need data from 2-3 services per query. Peak traffic is 100,000 GraphQL queries per second with complex nested resolves. The team wants to avoid managing GraphQL servers.
questions.questionText: Which architecture provides managed GraphQL with efficient multi-source resolution at this scale?

choices.text: AWS AppSync with pipeline resolvers, resolver-level caching, and VTL/JavaScript resolvers connecting to DynamoDB, Lambda, and HTTP data sources
EC2 instances running Apollo Server with DataLoader for batching and caching
API Gateway with Lambda resolvers implementing GraphQL schema manually
EKS with graphql-yoga and Redis caching layer for resolver results

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service provides fully managed GraphQL with built-in resolver caching and multiple data source types?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS AppSync is a fully managed GraphQL service that eliminates server management. Pipeline resolvers chain multiple data sources in a single field resolution — enabling aggregation from 2-3 services per resolve without custom orchestration code. Server-side caching at the resolver level reduces backend calls. AppSync supports DynamoDB, Lambda, HTTP, RDS, and OpenSearch as data sources — covering all 8 backend services. It auto-scales to handle 100K+ queries/second.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Pipeline resolvers execute a sequence of functions (AppSync Functions), each calling a different data source, passing context between them.
  • AppSync caching supports per-resolver TTLs and cache keys based on query arguments.
  • JavaScript resolvers (GA) replace VTL with familiar syntax for request/response mapping.
  • AppSync Merged APIs allow teams to own their portion of the schema independently and merge into a single endpoint.

questions.title: Database Performance Optimization
questions.scenario: A company's Aurora MySQL database handles 50,000 read queries and 5,000 write queries per second. Read latency has increased from 2ms to 15ms as the dataset grew to 2TB. The primary instance (r6g.4xlarge) shows 85% CPU utilization and 90% of the buffer pool is used. Adding read replicas has not improved latency for the most expensive queries which involve complex JOINs across 5 tables.
questions.questionText: Which optimization strategy addresses the root cause of read latency degradation?

choices.text: Scale up to r6g.8xlarge for more CPU and memory
Add more Aurora read replicas to distribute the read load
Implement read-through caching with ElastiCache for frequently accessed join results, add Aurora parallel query for complex analytics, and optimize indexes for the JOIN patterns
Migrate to Aurora Serverless v2 for automatic scaling

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Read replicas didn't help because the expensive queries are complex JOINs — the issue is query execution cost, not simple read distribution.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The root cause is complex JOIN queries hitting a buffer pool that cannot hold the working set of 5-table joins for a 2TB dataset. ElastiCache caches computed JOIN results — avoiding repeated expensive queries. Aurora Parallel Query offloads analytical queries to the storage layer, scanning data in parallel without consuming buffer pool. Proper composite indexes for the JOIN patterns (covering the WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY columns) reduce the data pages scanned. Read replicas have the same limitation — same data, same expensive query execution.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Aurora Parallel Query pushes predicate evaluation to the storage nodes — 5-table JOINs with WHERE clauses benefit massively.
  • ElastiCache read-through: cache key = query hash, value = result set. TTL based on data freshness requirements.
  • Buffer pool at 90% with 2TB data means significant page eviction — covering indexes reduce pages needed in memory.
  • Performance Insights can identify exactly which queries contribute most to load for targeted optimization.

questions.title: Compliance Boundary Architecture
questions.scenario: A government contractor must deploy applications meeting FedRAMP High requirements. Workloads process controlled unclassified information (CUI) and must be deployed only in GovCloud regions. They need to prevent accidental deployment to commercial regions, ensure all data is encrypted with FIPS 140-2 validated modules, and maintain continuous compliance evidence for annual audits.
questions.questionText: Which architecture enforces FedRAMP High compliance boundaries?

choices.text: Commercial AWS with encryption enabled and compliance documentation maintained manually

AWS GovCloud accounts with SCPs restricting actions to GovCloud regions only, FIPS endpoints enforced via IAM conditions, Config conformance packs for FedRAMP High, and Audit Manager for evidence collection
AWS GovCloud with manual compliance checks performed quarterly by the security team
Commercial AWS with a dedicated Organization and Control Tower for governance

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: FedRAMP High requires GovCloud plus FIPS endpoints plus continuous monitoring — which combination enforces all three?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS GovCloud is the FedRAMP High authorized environment. SCPs prevent any API calls to non-GovCloud regions (preventing data leakage to commercial). IAM conditions requiring aws:SecureTransport and FIPS endpoint usage ensure all API calls use FIPS 140-2 validated TLS modules. Config conformance packs continuously evaluate resources against FedRAMP High controls. Audit Manager automates evidence collection, mapping controls to AWS Config findings for the annual audit package.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• GovCloud FIPS endpoints: use fips.{service}.{region}.amazonaws.com for all API calls.
  • SCP condition "aws:RequestedRegion" can restrict to us-gov-west-1 and us-gov-east-1 only.
  • Config conformance packs include pre-built FedRAMP templates with 100+ rules mapped to NIST 800-53 controls.
  • Audit Manager custom frameworks can map to specific FedRAMP High control families (AC, AU, CM, IA, SC, etc.).

questions.title: Edge Computing Architecture
questions.scenario: A manufacturing company has 50 factories worldwide. Each factory generates 10GB of sensor data daily that must be processed locally for sub-millisecond control loop decisions. Only aggregated summaries (1% of raw data) should be sent to the cloud for global analytics. Factories have intermittent internet connectivity and must continue operating during outages lasting up to 48 hours.
questions.questionText: Which architecture provides local processing with cloud integration and offline resilience?

choices.text: AWS IoT Greengrass on local servers for edge ML inference and local processing, with store-and-forward to IoT Core when connectivity resumes, and S3 for global analytics
AWS Outposts rack in each factory for full AWS service availability locally
Direct Connect to each factory with all processing in the nearest AWS region
Snowball Edge devices permanently deployed for local compute with manual data shipping monthly

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which edge computing service provides local ML inference, operates during connectivity loss, and syncs to the cloud when connectivity returns?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: IoT Greengrass v2 runs on local servers, providing: local Lambda/container execution for sub-millisecond processing, ML inference using SageMaker Neo-compiled models, MQTT message broker for local device communication without cloud connectivity, and store-and-forward capability that queues messages during outages and syncs when connectivity resumes. Only aggregated summaries (configured via stream manager) are sent to IoT Core/S3. Outposts is overkill and requires reliable connectivity; Snowball Edge is designed for offline batch, not real-time control loops.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Greengrass stream manager handles local buffering with configurable retention (48+ hours) and bandwidth-aware upload policies.
  • Greengrass ML inference supports TensorFlow Lite, Apache MXNet, and PyTorch models compiled with SageMaker Neo.
  • Local MQTT broker enables device-to-device communication at microsecond latency without cloud round-trips.
  • Greengrass components are modular — deploy only needed capabilities (ML, stream manager, secret manager) per factory.

questions.title: Mainframe Modernization
questions.scenario: A bank runs a COBOL-based core banking system on an IBM mainframe processing 10 million transactions daily. They want to reduce mainframe MIPS costs by 60%. The application has 5 million lines of COBOL code. Complete rewrite is not feasible (estimated 5 years). They need to maintain transaction integrity (ACID) and existing batch processing schedules during migration.
questions.questionText: Which modernization approach achieves 60% cost reduction while preserving transaction integrity?

choices.text: Complete rewrite of all COBOL to Java microservices on EKS over 5 years
AWS Mainframe Modernization service with automated refactoring to convert COBOL to Java, running on managed runtime with existing batch schedules preserved
AWS Mainframe Modernization with replatform pattern — run COBOL code as-is on a Micro Focus runtime on AWS, reducing MIPS cost while preserving all existing logic and batch schedules
Keep the mainframe and optimize MIPS usage through workload redistribution only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: With 5M lines of COBOL and no feasible rewrite, which approach runs existing code on cheaper infrastructure while preserving behavior?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Mainframe Modernization with the replatform pattern runs existing COBOL code on Micro Focus (OpenFrame) runtime on AWS — no code changes required. This eliminates mainframe MIPS charges (60%+ cost reduction) while preserving all transaction integrity, batch schedules, and existing application behavior. The COBOL code, JCL batch jobs, CICS transactions, and DB2 calls continue working as-is. This is the lowest-risk path that achieves the cost target without a multi-year rewrite.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AWS Mainframe Modernization supports two patterns: Replatform (run COBOL as-is on Micro Focus) and Refactor (convert to Java via Blu Age).
  • Replatform preserves: COBOL programs, JCL batch jobs, CICS transaction processing, IMS/DB2 data access — all running on EC2.
  • Typical mainframe MIPS cost: $1,500-3,000/MIPS/year vs AWS equivalent compute at 60-80% less.
  • Batch scheduling is preserved using BMC Control-M or AWS Step Functions replacing mainframe job schedulers.
